newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says all warheads withdrawn from Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Russia says all warheads withdrawn from Belarus.

text.p: All warheads from former Soviet nuclear missiles deployed in Belarus have been sent to Russia, a spokesman for Moscow's strategic missile command said on Monday.
He made what he said was an official statement to counter confusion surrounding the scheduled withdrawal after a series of contradictory reports over the weekend.
"All the warheads have been withdrawn from Belarus. There is not a single one left," the spokesman told Reuters by telephone.

The move completes one of the major arms control tasks since the Cold War, concentrating on Russian territory the nuclear arsenal which found itself spread across four new independent states after the collapse of the Soviet Union.

On Friday, Belarus officials said the last missiles had left the republic's territory. But a spokesman for Minsk's Security Council told Interfax news agency late on Saturday that there were still 14 nuclear missiles in Belarus.
An official from the Russian strategic missile command, which is responsible for removing and decommissioning the missiles, said on Sunday the withdrawal was continuing.

The removal, under a deal that gave Russia control of the ex-Soviet nuclear arsenal, was due to be complete by the year's end. Missiles once located in Kazakhstan and Ukraine had already been withdrawn, leaving only those in Belarus outside Russia.

Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko, at loggerheads with his own parliament and Russia over plans to extend his powers, once threatened to keep a final 18 SS-25 strategic missiles as a bargaining chip against NATO's plans to expand eastwards.

Lukashenko said on Sunday that he understood the last missiles would leave on Tuesday, although he said it was up to those who would remove them -- that is the Russians. He said a ceremony would mark the transfer across the border.
"What Lukashenko said is what he said. We are making this official statement," the strategic command spokesman said on Monday. "Perhaps he mixed something up."

Russian news agencies quoted the strategic command as saying there had been 18 nuclear missiles in Belarus and that the remaining parts of the missiles and their launching equipment would be removed by the end of the year.
Russia has been mediating in the conflict between Lukashenko and his parliament over a referendum on Sunday which the authorities said gave him a mandate to extend his powers.

Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, who flew to Minsk on Thursday for all night crisis talks, expressed irritation with Lukashenko on Sunday that the accord he brokered to end the standoff had collapsed within a day.
Belarus, a republic of 10 million bordering Russia and Poland, was the only former Soviet state outside Russia still to have missiles on its soil.
Interfax news agency quoted the head of the Strategic Missile Command, General Viktor Yesin, as saying the withdrawal completed the removal of the ex-Soviet missiles.

"The completion of the transportation of the warheads remaining in Belarus marks the fulfillment by the Russian strategic command of the removal of nuclear warheads from the CIS states where they were previously deployed," he said.
